question: A man, a woman and a boy can complete a work in 3, 4 and 12 days, respectively. How many boys must assist one man and one woman to complete the same work in one day?
solution:
**Given:**

A man, a woman, and a boy can complete a work in 3, 4, and 12 days

**Concept used:**

Efficiency = Total work/time taken

For this type of question, we take LCM of time taken by the individual people.

**Calculation:**

LCM of 3, 4, and 12 is 12

Let the total work be 12 units

So, efficiency of a man = 12/3 = 4 units/ day

Efficiency of a woman = 12/4 = 3 units/ day

Efficiency of a boy = 12/12 = 1 units/ day

To complete the whole work in one day the effective efficiency must be 12

So, effective efficiency of a man and woman = 4 + 3 = 7 units

Now, remaining = 12 - 7 = 5

So, number of boys = 5/1 = 5

**∴ 5 boys must assist one man and one woman to complete the same work in one day.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**Man's 1 day work = 1/3

Woman's 1 day work = 1/4

Boy's 1 day work = 1/12

According to question-

⇒ 1 × (1/3) + 1 × (1/4) + x × (1/12) = 1 { ∵ x be the no. of boys needed} 

⇒ x/12 = 1 - (1/3) - (1/4)

⇒ x/12 = (12 - 7)/12

⇒ x = 5

∴ **5 Boys are needed to complete the work.**
